label: refute-f6-examples
tail:
LOCATION: Facts & Assumptions [L1], line 72; used in Verification 1.3, line 98  
QUOTE: "[L1] $\mathbb{R}$ is a complete ordered field with a total order ([[def-real-numbers]], [[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[def-real-order]]), hence Archimedean ([[thm-of-archimedean]]), and $\iota : \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{R}$ is the unique order-preserving field embedding ([[lem-of-q-embeds]])."  
DEFECT: The cited definitions construct the reals, define their order, and define what a complete ordered field is; they do not prove that the constructed reals are totally ordered or complete. Thus the premise needed to invoke the Archimedean theorem is unsupported, as is the totality used in step 1.3.  
EVIDENCE: The cited def-real-numbers Definition says only that the reals are the quotient ring of Cauchy sequences by null sequences. The missing on-disk results are thm-reals-ordered-field, titled “The reals form a totally ordered field”, and cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete, titled “The Cauchy-sequence reals have the least-upper-bound property”.  
SEVERITY: fatal  
MINIMAL REPAIR: Add the on-disk ordered-field and least-upper-bound results to deps and cite them in [L1].

### FINDING 3 — ex-an-aleph-fixed-point — undisclosed use of choice in the cardinal-power comparison

LOCATION: Example, lines 48–53; repeated in Remarks, line 97  
QUOTE: "The power operation behaves differently: $\kappa < 2^{\kappa}$ at every cardinal ([[thm-cardinal-power-set-and-cantor]]), so there are no fixed points there at all."  
DEFECT: The item declares that it works in ZF without choice, but this comparison uses cardinal exponentiation at every cardinal. Under the library definition, that operation is not globally available in ZF, and the cited theorem assumes the Axiom of Choice. The final Remark repeats the same undisclosed dependence through the cofinality-of-a-cardinal-power corollary.  
EVIDENCE: The Statement of thm-cardinal-power-set-and-cantor begins “Assume the Axiom of Choice”. The Statement of cor-cofinality-of-a-cardinal-power carries the same hypothesis.  
SEVERITY: fatal  
MINIMAL REPAIR: Qualify both cardinal-power claims with “Assuming the Axiom of Choice,” and add the two cited results to deps.

### FINDING 4 — ex-the-beth-hierarchy-computed — title omits the essential choice hypothesis

LOCATION: Frontmatter title, line 4  
QUOTE: "title: \"$\\beth_0 = \\aleph_0$, $\\beth_1 = 2^{\\aleph_0} = \\lvert \\mathbb{R} \\rvert$, $\\beth_2 = \\lvert \\mathcal{P}(\\mathbb{R}) \\rvert$, and $\\beth_\\omega$ has cofinality $\\aleph_0$\""  
DEFECT: The title states the beth computations unconditionally, while both the proof and the library’s beth definition require the Axiom of Choice. It therefore asserts more than the proof establishes.  
EVIDENCE: The item begins, “**Assume the Axiom of Choice** ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), which is what makes the beths available at all ([[def-aleph-and-beth-hierarchies]]).” The cited definition says, “**The beths**, assuming the Axiom of Choice, are the parallel operation”.  
SEVERITY: fatal  
MINIMAL REPAIR: Prefix the title with “Assuming the Axiom of Choice,”.

### FINDING 5 — ex-counting-functions-and-subsets-of-the-continuum — title omits the essential choice hypothesis

LOCATION: Frontmatter title, line 4  
QUOTE: "title: \"$\\aleph_0^{\\aleph_0} = 2^{\\aleph_0}$ and $\\lvert \\mathbb{R}^{\\mathbb{R}} \\rvert = 2^{2^{\\aleph_0}}$, computed from the exponent laws and Hessenberg\""  
DEFECT: The title states cardinal exponentials and the cardinality of the real function space without qualification, but the proof assumes the Axiom of Choice to ensure that all these cardinalities and exponentials exist. The title therefore exceeds the proved claim.  
EVIDENCE: The body states, “**Assume the Axiom of Choice** ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).” Its Given clause says, “**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, so that every exponential below is defined ([[def-cardinal-arithmetic]], [[thm-well-ordering-theorem]]).”  
SEVERITY: fatal  
MINIMAL REPAIR: Prefix the title with “Assuming the Axiom of Choice,”.
